_comment: Shared vectors for how a SwipeActions row follows a pointer and where it comes to rest
(CoreSwipeGeometry.constrain / settle / targetOf, CoreSwipeDrag, CoreSwipeGesture,
CoreSwipeActionsStyle.extentFor).
Read by coui_core (every section, against the engine), coui_flutter (every gestures row is
replayed on the SwipeActions widget as real pointer events, so the framework's drag
recogniser has to answer the table), coui_web (every gestures row is replayed on the row's
pointer model with a manual clock) and a real-Chrome probe of the Web row (a subset, with
real pointer input). A rule that changes on one platform fails the other.
UNITS. Positions, offsets and extents are logical px (CSS px on the Web). Velocities are
logical px per SECOND, signed like positions (positive = toward the right). Times are ms.
SIGNS. Every offset in this table is PHYSICAL: positive is toward the right, whatever the
reading direction. 'rtl': true makes the leading actions the ones on the right, so they are
revealed by moving the row LEFT (negative). The engine flips the sign in exactly one place.
numbers: the Contract figures the table is stated for, so a change to one of them fails here
before it fails anywhere else. style: the cell, spacing and inset the extents are derived from.
row: the row the gestures are replayed on (width, height); pointer coordinates are in the row's
own box, from its top-left.
extent: the platter width of 'count' cells (CoreSwipeActionsStyle.extentFor); actionWidth,
actionSpacing and platterInset default to the 'style' block.
constrain: the row's offset when the pointer would carry it to 'raw', the offset the drag
started at plus the pointer's travel since it armed. 'leading' / 'trailing' are platter
widths in px (0 = no actions on that side). leadingFullSwipe / trailingFullSwipe default to
true. lockedSide is the side that was open when the drag began.
settle: what releasing at 'offset' with 'velocity' does, and the offset it rests at ('target').
A platter that already reaches the full-swipe distance runs its first action only after a pull of
'fullSwipeOvershoot' beyond it; a platter short of that distance never reads the figure.
'executeLeading' / 'executeTrailing' run the first action of that side, then rest at 0.
open: where a row rests when a side is opened without a pointer - keyboard focus reaching
one of its actions (CoreSwipeGeometry.openOffsetOf). 'leading' / 'trailing' are NUMBERS OF
ACTIONS, as in 'gestures'; 'side' is the side that opens and 'offset' the physical offset the
row rests at, the target of that side's open outcome.
gestures: a pointer trace replayed on a row of the stated action counts ('leading' /
'trailing' are NUMBERS OF ACTIONS here, not px; their platters are extentFor of that many
cells). 'startOffset' is the row's offset before the press (an open row). events are down,
move, up and cancel with a time 'at' and a position (x, y). 'offsets' is the row's offset after
each move event, in order; 'release' is what the lift (or cancel) decided, null when the
press was a tap or went vertical. The slop forgives the first 18 px: the row does not move on
the move that arms the drag. The strokes keep a wide margin either side of the 400 px/s fling
velocity (flicks run at about 1200 px/s, slow drags well under 100), because the Flutter
recogniser measures its own velocity: a flick is only a flick when both estimators say so.

extent.name: one cell: the cell and an inset at each end
two cells add a cell and a spacing
a style states its own cell, spacing and inset

constrain.name: within the leading platter the row follows the pointer exactly
exactly the platter's width is still one to one
past the platter with full swipe on the row keeps following
...as far as the row's own width and no further
trailing mirrors leading: within the platter
trailing: past the platter with full swipe on
full swipe off: past the platter the row resists, a quarter of the excess
full swipe off, trailing: the excess is the pull beyond 72
full swipe off: within the platter nothing resists
a side with no actions does not move
...whichever side it is
started with leading open: a pull back across closed stops at closed
started with leading open: pulled to exactly closed is closed
started with trailing open: a pull across to leading stops at closed
started with trailing open: its own side is free
right to left: the leading platter is revealed by moving left
right to left: the trailing platter is revealed by moving right
right to left: past the leading platter with full swipe on
right to left: a lock on leading stops a pull right at closed
right to left, full swipe off: the same resistance, mirrored
a row narrower than its platter still follows within the platter
...and past it holds at the platter, not at the row

settle.name: a closed row stays closed
a row within a pixel of closed is closed, whatever the speed
less than half the platter out rests closed
exactly half the platter out rests open
trailing: half of 72 is 36, and 35 rests closed
trailing: 36 rests open at the platter's width
a flick toward the actions opens them however short the pull
exactly the fling velocity is a flick
a pixel per second under it is not
a flick away from the actions closes however far out
exactly the fling velocity away is a flick
a pixel per second under it, far out, still rests open
trailing: a flick toward the actions is a negative velocity
trailing: a flick back toward the edge closes
past the platter, short of the full-swipe distance, rests open
at the full-swipe distance (65% of 400 = 260) the first action runs
a pixel short of it rests open
trailing: the full-swipe distance is the same share of the row
a flick back cancels even a pull past the full-swipe distance
a flick toward the actions past the distance still runs the action
full swipe off: a long pull only opens
full swipe is per side: trailing off, leading still runs
...and trailing only opens
a side with no actions is closed, whatever the offset
right to left: the leading platter is on the left of zero
right to left: a flick toward leading is a negative velocity
right to left: the full-swipe pull is negative for leading
right to left: the trailing platter opens to the right
a row narrower than its platter opens at the platter's width
...and a pull one pixel past it is still an opening
...and runs the first action once the pull is the overshoot past it
a platter past the full-swipe distance: one pixel beyond it only opens
...and the first action waits for the overshoot
...and runs there
a flick toward the actions short of the overshoot still only opens
trailing reads the same distance
...and runs there too

open.name: the leading platter opens to its width
the trailing platter opens to minus its width
one action: the cell and an inset at each end
right to left: the leading platter opens to the left
right to left: the trailing platter opens to the right
right to left, three actions: the trailing platter opens to the right

gestures.name: a slow pull past half the trailing platter opens it
a slow short pull rests closed
a quick flick opens although the pull is short
a flick held still before the lift is not a flick
a quick flick back closes an open row
a slow pull back past half closes an open row
a slow small pull back leaves an open row open
full swipe off: past the platter the row resists and a release opens
full swipe: a pull to the threshold runs the first trailing action
a pixel short of the threshold opens instead
a slow pull toward the end opens the leading platter
a pull toward a side with no actions does not move the row
a stroke that goes down first belongs to the scroller
a press that never leaves the slop is a tap
right to left: the leading platter opens by pulling left
right to left: the trailing platter opens by pulling right
a drag that starts with leading open cannot swing across to trailing
a cancelled pull goes back and never runs an action
a cancelled pull on an open row goes back to open
exactly the slop is still a press; a pixel more is a drag
